name: manual_129c8d
claim: When publishing a reapplied delta with an expected-head compare-and-set, capture the expected SHA once immediately after the initial fetch and reuse it unchanged; before the push require git merge-base --is-ancestor EXPECTED HEAD. An explicit force-with-lease branch:sha lease checks only the remote value and still permits a non-fast-forward update, so it cannot prove the tip contains the head it authorises replacing; re-resolving the tracking ref after the reapply can name a commit the tip lacks.

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review 5510696885 on orama-system PR 404, 2026-10-14 (PHT) / 2026-10-13 UTC: the reapply card's publish examples re-resolved origin/BRANCH after the reapply and relied on the lease alone. Verified against git-push semantics. Refines lesson_590ae6342a41 (expected-head CAS); does not supersede it.
